scenes.title: The outcome
points: Reuse local and SSH machines as workers
Keep private endpoints out of the repo
Real session excerpts; edited transcript replay

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Do I need to buy runners or move my code into a hosted service?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: No new fleet is required. This course connects machines you already own to Literate AI as workers. The key boundary is simple: the project declares what it needs, while your private user configuration chooses where work runs. These are edited transcript replays of real sessions, not raw screen recordings. Remote-worker steps are a walkthrough.

scenes.title: Target versus worker
points: --target selects intended platform and Flavors
--worker selects the execution endpoint
Omitting --worker selects implicit local

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Why not just put the SSH host in my project file?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Because endpoints and credentials are private execution choices, not portable product authority. A target and a worker are different decisions. The target determines the recipe and intended platform; the worker is the local, command, or SSH endpoint that executes it. Never encode private hostnames in project specifications.

scenes.title: Find private config paths
points: Use platform-resolved paths from the CLI
Keep worker and test files outside Git

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Ask litai config paths where this platform stores user configuration. Copy the checked-in synthetic examples to those private locations, or pass explicit absolute paths. Do not guess Windows or Unix conventions from memory.

scenes.title: Define a worker
points: Start with a worker ID and exact OS
Add the SSH endpoint and workspace privately
Leave unused hardware qualifiers unset

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: In your private workers file, replace each example endpoint and workspace with a real assignment. Give each machine a stable worker ID and exact platform requirements. Keep credentials out of this JSON file.

scenes.title: Choose a matrix
points: Select worker IDs, not duplicated endpoints
Pair each worker with a matching OS Flavor
Select a coding CLI and resolvable model

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: The test matrix selects workers by ID and matching platform Flavor. It also selects a coding CLI and model for live generation. The matrix does not repeat SSH credentials or provisioning commands.

scenes.title: Verify model and machine
points: A model alias must resolve in the chosen CLI
Probe current OS, CPU, memory, and GPU facts
Degraded is not the same as absent

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: My model name works in chat. Why verify it again?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Verify the model before a long run, then probe every configured worker. A missing NVIDIA utility means no GPU was discovered; a utility that cannot query its driver is a degraded observation, not proof of zero devices.

scenes.title: Prepare the worker
points: Check toolchain before installing anything
Use exact Git checkout, submodules, and LFS
Authenticate the coding CLI separately

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Prepare each assigned machine with detect-before-install checks. Hydrate the exact Git revision, including required submodules and LFS content. Coding-agent login is a separate readiness gate, and secrets stay in the worker environment.

scenes.title: Run one cell first
points: Start with one sample and one platform
Expand only after source and toolchain checks pass
Worker evidence returns to the coordinator

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Start with one sample and one worker cell. Only expand the matrix after platform, source authority, and toolchain preflight pass. For this repository, samples-platform-regression is the supported fan-out demonstration.

scenes.title: Use a worker directly
points: Single-Component lifecycle accepts --worker ID
Artifacts and receipts are content-bound
A remote path alone is not accepted evidence

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: If the remote machine says it passed, why isn't that enough?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: For a single Component, build, test, and run can choose a configured worker by ID. Returned artifacts and receipts must be imported and verified by the coordinator; a path on another machine alone is not evidence.

scenes.title: Actual local worker run
points: The starter wheel built on the implicit local worker
Result reports worker_id: local
SSH workers need your private endpoints

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Our real package build used the implicit local worker and produced a pip wheel. That verifies the local execution path without exposing a host address. To demonstrate an SSH worker, configure one of your own machines privately and rerun the same target with its worker ID.

scenes.title: What to expect
points: Parallelize eligible cells across existing hardware
Keep capacity observations separate from requirements
Do not claim generic fan-out for derived projects

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: This can make cross-platform tests more practical without buying a new service. Capacity probes inform selection, but never rewrite authored minimum requirements. Derived projects can wire the private matrix into their own CI; the packaged CLI does not promise a generic fan-out verb.
